An ammeter is used to measure current and is connected in series in a circuit. To ensure it does not significantly alter the current it is measuring, it must have a very low resistance.

A voltmeter is used to measure potential difference and is connected in parallel across the component. To ensure it draws negligible current from the circuit, it must have a very high resistance.

Therefore, the statement that a voltmeter has a low resistance and an ammeter has a high resistance is incorrect.

Answer: A voltmeter has a low resistance and an ammeter has a high resistance

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: At uniform speed the acceleration is
questions.solution:
Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time, $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt}$.

When a body moves with a uniform speed in a straight line, its velocity is constant.

Since the velocity is constant, the change in velocity is zero.

Therefore, the acceleration of the body is zero.

Answer: Zero

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The focal length of a concave lens is 0·5 m. The power of the lens is
questions.solution:
The focal length of a concave lens is taken as negative.

$f = -0\cdot5$ m

The power of a lens is given by $P = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$P = \dfrac{1}{-0\cdot5} = -2\cdot0$ D

Answer: −2·0 D

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: If three resistors of 1 Ohm each connect in parallel to each other the resultant resistance is
questions.solution:
For resistors connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance $R_{eq}$ is given by:

$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} + \dfrac{1}{R_3}$

Given $R_1 = R_2 = R_3 = 1 \Omega$, substituting the values:

$\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{1} + \dfrac{1}{1} + \dfrac{1}{1} = 3$

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{1}{3} \Omega$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$ Ohm

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The rule to determine the direction of a force experienced by a straight current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it is
questions.solution:
Fleming's left-hand rule is used to determine the direction of the force experienced by a straight current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.

According to this rule, if the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the left hand are stretched mutually perpendicular to each other, such that the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger points in the direction of the current, then the thumb gives the direction of the force experienced by the conductor.

The right-hand thumb rule is used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.

Fleming's right-hand rule is used to determine the direction of induced current.

Hund's rule is a principle of atomic chemistry related to the filling of electrons in orbitals.

Answer: Fleming's left-hand rule

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: One parsec in astronomical units (A.U.) is about
questions.solution:
One parsec is defined as the distance at which an arc of length one astronomical unit (A.U.) subtends an angle of one second of arc.

$\theta = 1'' = \left(\dfrac{1}{3600}\right)^\circ = \dfrac{\pi}{180 \times 3600} \text{ rad}$

$r = \dfrac{l}{\theta} = \dfrac{1 \text{ A.U.}}{\dfrac{\pi}{180 \times 3600}}$

$r = \dfrac{180 \times 3600}{\pi} \text{ A.U.} \approx 206265 \text{ A.U.}$

$r \approx 2 \times 10^5 \text{ A.U.}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^5$ A.U.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A car has an initial velocity of 12 m/s and is brought to rest over a distance of 45 m. The acceleration of the car is
questions.solution:
Given initial velocity $u = 12$ m/s.

Final velocity $v = 0$ m/s.

Distance covered $s = 45$ m.

Using the third equation of motion:

$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$

Substituting the given values:

$0 = (12)^2 + 2a(45)$

$0 = 144 + 90a$

$90a = -144$

$a = -\dfrac{144}{90}$

$a = -1.6$ m/s$^2$

Answer: $-1.6$ m/s$^2$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The magnetic field inside a long straight solenoid-carrying current
options: decreases as we move towards its end
increases as we move towards its end
questions.solution:
The magnetic field lines inside a long straight solenoid carrying current are in the form of parallel straight lines. This indicates that the magnetic field is the same at all points inside the solenoid.

The magnitude of the magnetic field inside an ideal long solenoid is given by $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $I$ is the current. Since $\mu_0$, $n$, and $I$ are constant, the magnetic field is uniform inside the solenoid.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements for second law of motion is NOT correct?
options: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's acceleration
The net force on a body is in the same direction as the acceleration
The time rate of change of momentum is equal to force
The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum
questions.solution:
According to Newton's second law of motion, the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.

Mathematically, $\vec{F} = \dfrac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$.

For a body of constant mass, $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$. This implies that the net force is proportional to the acceleration and acts in the same direction as the acceleration.

The net force is proportional to the time rate of change of momentum, not to the momentum itself. Therefore, the statement that the net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum is incorrect.

Answer: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements for the work done by gravity on a body is NOT correct?
options: Work done is independent of the path followed by the body
Work done depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and the final position of the body
Work done depends on the path followed by the body
Work done is zero if the body is displaced horizontally to the force of gravity
questions.solution:
The gravitational force is a conservative force.

For any conservative force, the work done is independent of the path taken and depends only on the initial and final positions of the body.

Specifically for gravity, the work done is given by $W = mgh$, where $h$ is the vertical displacement. Thus, it depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and final positions.

If the displacement is purely horizontal, the angle between the gravitational force (downwards) and the displacement is $90^{\circ}$. The work done is $W = Fd \cos(90^{\circ}) = 0$.

Therefore, the statement that work done depends on the path followed by the body is incorrect.

Answer: Work done depends on the path followed by the body

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The temperature of a body increases from 310 K to 340 K. The temperature increase in degree Celsius is
questions.solution:
Initial temperature, $T_1 = 310$ K

Final temperature, $T_2 = 340$ K

Change in temperature, $\Delta T = T_2 - T_1 = 340 - 310 = 30$ K

Since the size of one degree on the Celsius scale is equal to the size of one unit on the Kelvin scale, the change in temperature in degree Celsius is equal to the change in temperature in Kelvin.

$\Delta T = 30^{\circ}\text{C}$

Answer: 30°C

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Two bodies of unequal masses are dropped from a tower. At any instant, they have equal
questions.solution:
When two bodies are dropped from a height, they fall freely under gravity.

The acceleration of a freely falling body is the acceleration due to gravity $g$, which is independent of the mass of the body.

Therefore, both bodies will have the same acceleration at any instant.

Momentum $p = mv$, kinetic energy $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$, and potential energy $U = mgh$ all depend on the mass $m$ of the body.

Since the masses are unequal, their momentum, kinetic energy, and potential energy will be different.

Answer : Acceleration

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following statements is correct?
options: Pressure has magnitude as well as direction
As we go deeper in a liquid, the pressure decreases
Action and reaction forces act on the same object
Pascal and N/m$^2$ represent the same unit
questions.solution:
Pressure is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no specific direction, as it acts equally in all directions at a point in a fluid.

As depth in a liquid increases, the pressure increases according to the relation $P = P_0 + \rho g h$.

According to Newton's third law of motion, action and reaction forces always act on two different objects.

The SI unit of pressure is defined as force per unit area, which is $\text{N/m}^2$. This unit is also known as Pascal (Pa). Therefore, Pascal and $\text{N/m}^2$ represent the same unit.

Answer: Pascal and N/m$^2$ represent the same unit

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The energy, $E$, of a photon can be expressed as $E = hf$ where $f$ is the frequency and $h$ is Planck's constant. The dimensions of $h$ are the same as that of
questions.solution:
$E = hf$

$[h] = \dfrac{[E]}{[f]}$

Substituting the dimensions of energy $[E] = [M L^2 T^{-2}]$ and frequency $[f] = [T^{-1}]$:

$[h] = \dfrac{[M L^2 T^{-2}]}{[T^{-1}]} = [M L^2 T^{-1}]$

Dimensions of angular momentum $L = mvr$ are $[M][L T^{-1}][L] = [M L^2 T^{-1}]$.

Therefore, the dimensions of Planck's constant are the same as that of angular momentum.

Answer: angular momentum

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following wavelength radiations may correspond to an X-ray?
questions.solution:
The wavelength range of X-rays in the electromagnetic spectrum is generally from $0.01 \text{ nm}$ to $10 \text{ nm}$ (or $0.1 \text{ \AA}$ to $100 \text{ \AA}$).

Among the given options, $1 \text{ nm}$ falls well within the characteristic wavelength range of X-rays.

Wavelengths from $10 \text{ nm}$ to $400 \text{ nm}$ correspond to the ultraviolet region.

Answer: 1 nm

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The magnetic field inside a current carrying very long solenoid is
questions.solution:
For a very long current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field at any point well inside it is given by $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space, $n$ is the number of turns per unit length, and $I$ is the steady current.

Since the parameters $n$ and $I$ are constant, the magnetic field has a constant magnitude. Furthermore, the direction of the magnetic field is parallel to the axis of the solenoid throughout its interior.

Therefore, the magnetic field inside a very long solenoid is uniform.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The temperature at which "vapour pressure of the liquid in an open vessel becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure" is called
questions.solution:
The boiling point of a liquid is defined as the temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure.

At this temperature, bubbles of vapour form within the bulk of the liquid and escape into the atmosphere.

Answer: Boiling point

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about surface tension is correct?
options: It will remain same with increase or decrease of temperature
It will always decrease with increase or decrease of temperature
questions.solution:
Surface tension is the property of a liquid that arises due to intermolecular forces of attraction between its molecules.

When the temperature of a liquid increases, the kinetic energy of its molecules also increases.

This increased kinetic energy helps to overcome the intermolecular forces of attraction, leading to a decrease in the cohesive forces between the molecules.

Consequently, the surface tension of the liquid decreases with an increase in temperature. At the critical temperature, the surface tension becomes zero.

Answer: It decreases when temperature increases

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A body sinks in water when
options: density of water is greater than density of body
density of water is less than density of body
density of water is equal to density of body
questions.solution:
A body sinks in a liquid if the buoyant force acting on it is less than its weight.

This occurs when the density of the body is greater than the density of the liquid.

Therefore, a body sinks in water when the density of water is less than the density of the body.

Answer: density of water is less than density of body

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Why a fielder in the ground gradually pulls his hands backward while catching a fast moving cricket ball?
options: To reduce the acceleration of the ball
To increase the acceleration of the ball
To increase the velocity of the ball
questions.solution:
When a fielder pulls his hands backward while catching a fast-moving cricket ball, the time taken to bring the ball to rest is increased.

Since acceleration is the rate of change of velocity ($a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$), increasing the time interval $\Delta t$ decreases the magnitude of acceleration.

According to Newton's second law of motion ($F = ma$), a smaller acceleration results in a smaller impact force exerted on the fielder's hands, thereby preventing injury.

Therefore, the fielder pulls his hands backward to reduce the acceleration of the ball.

Answer: To reduce the acceleration of the ball

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: When a light ray passes through from air to water with a non-zero angle the ray will be
questions.solution:
When a light ray travels from an optically rarer medium (air) to an optically denser medium (water), its speed decreases.

According to Snell's law, $\mu_1 \sin i = \mu_2 \sin r$.

Since the refractive index of water is greater than that of air ($\mu_2 \gt \mu_1$), we have $\sin r \lt \sin i$, which implies $r \lt i$.

Thus, the refracted ray bends towards the normal.

Answer: bending towards the normal

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Bottom of a tank containing water appears to be raised. It is due to
questions.solution:
When light rays travel from a denser medium (water) to a rarer medium (air), they bend away from the normal at the interface. This phenomenon is known as refraction of light.

Due to this bending, the virtual image of the bottom of the tank is formed above the actual bottom, making the apparent depth less than the real depth. Hence, the bottom of the tank appears to be raised.

Answer: Refraction of light

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following radiations has longer wavelength?
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic spectrum in the order of increasing wavelength is:

Gamma rays < X-rays < Ultraviolet < Visible light < Infrared < Microwaves < Radio waves.

Comparing the given options, microwaves have the longest wavelength.

Answer: Micro Wave

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: SONAR stands for
questions.solution:
SONAR stands for Sound Navigation and Ranging. It is a technique that uses sound propagation to navigate, communicate with, or detect objects on or under the surface of the water.

Answer: Sound Navigation and Ranging

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: We hear an echo due to
questions.solution:
An echo is the phenomenon of hearing a sound again after it has been reflected from a distant obstacle such as a wall, mountain, or building.

Therefore, an echo is caused by the reflection of sound waves.

Answer: Reflection of sound waves

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant object distinctly, the person is suffering with
questions.solution:
The defect of vision in which a person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly is known as near-sightedness or myopia.

In this condition, the far point of the eye shifts closer than infinity, and the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina instead of on it.

Therefore, the person is suffering from myopia.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The energy is always conserved for a system which is
questions.solution:
According to the law of conservation of energy, the total energy of an isolated system remains constant over time.

For a non-isolated system, energy can be exchanged with the surroundings in the form of work, heat, or matter, meaning the energy of the system itself is not conserved.

Thus, energy is always conserved for an isolated system only.

Answer: isolated only

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Suppose, a ball of mass M is thrown upwards from a point A and it reaches up to the highest point B and returns back to point A, which one among the following is correct?
options: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at B
Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at A
Kinetic Energy at B = Potential Energy at B
Kinetic Energy at B = Kinetic Energy at A
questions.solution:
Let the reference level for potential energy be at point A. Thus, the potential energy at A is zero.

When the ball is thrown upwards from point A with velocity $v$, its kinetic energy is $\dfrac{1}{2}Mv^2$.

Total mechanical energy at A is $E_A = \dfrac{1}{2}Mv^2 + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}Mv^2$.

At the highest point B, the velocity of the ball becomes zero, so its kinetic energy at B is zero.

Let the height of point B from A be $h$. The potential energy at B is $Mgh$.

Total mechanical energy at B is $E_B = 0 + Mgh = Mgh$.

According to the law of conservation of mechanical energy, the total energy at A equals the total energy at B.

$E_A = E_B \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}Mv^2 = Mgh$

Therefore, the kinetic energy at A is equal to the potential energy at B.

Answer: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at B

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The reaction that occurs on passing carbon dioxide gas through lime water is
questions.solution:
Lime water is an aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, $Ca(OH)_2$.

When carbon dioxide gas is passed through lime water, it reacts with calcium hydroxide to form a white precipitate of calcium carbonate and water.

The chemical equation for this reaction is:
$Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 + H_2O$

Answer: $Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 + H_2O$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Water of crystallization is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt
The molecular formula of Plaster of Paris is $CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$
Washing soda is used for removing the permanent hardness of water
The atmosphere of Venus is made up of thick white and yellow clouds of sulphuric acid
questions.solution:
Water of crystallization is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt. This statement is correct.

The chemical formula of Plaster of Paris is $CaSO_4 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}H_2O$ (calcium sulphate hemihydrate). The formula $CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$ represents gypsum. Thus, this statement is incorrect.

Washing soda ($Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O$) is used for removing the permanent hardness of water by precipitating calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble carbonates. This statement is correct.

The atmosphere of Venus is made up of thick white and yellow clouds of sulphuric acid. This statement is correct.

Answer: The molecular formula of Plaster of Paris is $CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT present in cement?
questions.solution:
Portland cement is a complex mixture of silicates and aluminates of calcium.

The main constituents of Portland cement are:
Dicalcium silicate ($2CaO \cdot SiO_2$)
Tricalcium silicate ($3CaO \cdot SiO_2$)
Tricalcium aluminate ($3CaO \cdot Al_2O_3$)
Tetracalcium aluminoferrite ($4CaO \cdot Al_2O_3 \cdot Fe_2O_3$)

Tetracalcium silicate ($4CaO \cdot SiO_2$) is not a constituent of cement.

Answer: $4CaO \cdot SiO_2$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a chemical change?
questions.solution:
A chemical change involves the formation of one or more new substances with different chemical properties.

Burning of coal is a combustion reaction, which is a chemical change.

Rusting of metal is an oxidation reaction, which is a chemical change.

Reaction of an acid with a base is a neutralization reaction, which is a chemical change.

Melting of ice is a change of state from solid to liquid. The chemical composition of water remains the same ($H_2O$). Therefore, it is a physical change and not a chemical change.

Answer: Melting of ice

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: The interconversion of states of matter is a physical change
During burning of a candle, both chemical and physical changes take place
During a physical change, the chemical composition of molecules changes
Rusting of iron is a chemical change
questions.solution:
A physical change is a change in which no new substance is formed and the chemical composition of the substance remains exactly the same.

The interconversion of states of matter (such as melting of ice or boiling of water) does not alter the chemical composition of the substance, hence it is a physical change.

During the burning of a candle, the melting of wax is a physical change, while the combustion of wax to form carbon dioxide and water vapor is a chemical change. Thus, both physical and chemical changes take place.

Rusting of iron involves the reaction of iron with oxygen and moisture to form a new chemical compound, hydrated iron(III) oxide. Therefore, it is a chemical change.

Since the chemical composition of molecules does not change during a physical change, the statement in option (3) is incorrect.

Answer: During a physical change, the chemical composition of molecules changes

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture?
options: Mixture of sugar and salt crystals
questions.solution:
Sulphur is a non-polar solid and carbon disulphide ($CS_2$) is a non-polar solvent.

According to the principle of like dissolves like, sulphur dissolves completely in carbon disulphide to form a true solution.

A true solution is a homogeneous mixture, not a heterogeneous mixture.

Mixture of sugar and salt crystals, sandy water, and sulphur in water do not form true solutions and are heterogeneous mixtures.

Answer: Sulphur in carbon disulphide

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I (Element)List II (Atomicity)
A. Phosphorus1. 2
B. Nitrogen2. 1
C. Neon3. 8
D. Sulphur4. 4
questions.solution:
Atomicity is the number of atoms present in one molecule of an element.

Phosphorus exists as $P_4$ molecules. Its atomicity is 4. Thus, A matches with 4.

Nitrogen exists as $N_2$ molecules. Its atomicity is 2. Thus, B matches with 1.

Neon is a noble gas and exists as monatomic $Ne$. Its atomicity is 1. Thus, C matches with 2.

Sulphur exists as $S_8$ molecules. Its atomicity is 8. Thus, D matches with 3.

The correct matching is A-4, B-1, C-2, D-3.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: In a Telescope, compared to the eyepiece lens the objective lens has
options: larger focal length and larger aperture
larger focal length and smaller aperture
smaller focal length and larger aperture
smaller focal length and smaller aperture
questions.solution:
In a telescope, the objective lens is designed to collect as much light as possible from distant objects to form a bright image. Therefore, it must have a large aperture.

The magnifying power of a telescope in normal adjustment is given by $M = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$, where $f_o$ is the focal length of the objective and $f_e$ is the focal length of the eyepiece. To achieve high magnification, the focal length of the objective lens must be much larger than that of the eyepiece.

Thus, the objective lens has a larger focal length and a larger aperture compared to the eyepiece lens.

Answer: larger focal length and larger aperture

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
In the following redox reaction, which compound is acting as a reducing agent?
$N_2H_4 + 2H_2O_2 \rightarrow N_2 + 4H_2O$
questions.solution:
In the given reaction, the oxidation state of nitrogen in $N_2H_4$ is $-2$ and it changes to $0$ in $N_2$. Since the oxidation state of nitrogen increases, $N_2H_4$ undergoes oxidation.

The oxidation state of oxygen in $H_2O_2$ is $-1$ and it changes to $-2$ in $H_2O$. Since the oxidation state of oxygen decreases, $H_2O_2$ undergoes reduction.

The species that undergoes oxidation acts as a reducing agent. Therefore, $N_2H_4$ is the reducing agent.

Answer: $N_2H_4$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The work done by the force acting on an object is zero if the displacement of the object
options: is in the opposite direction of the direction of force
is in the same direction of the direction of force
is in perpendicular direction of the direction of force
questions.solution:
Work done by a force is given by the dot product of force and displacement vectors.

$W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{s} = F s \cos \theta$

where $\theta$ is the angle between the force vector $\vec{F}$ and the displacement vector $\vec{s}$.

For work done to be zero, $\cos \theta$ must be zero, which implies $\theta = 90^{\circ}$.

Thus, the work done is zero when the displacement of the object is in a direction perpendicular to the direction of the force.

Answer: is in perpendicular direction of the direction of force

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is considered to be the purest source of water?
questions.solution:
Rain water is considered to be the purest form of natural water. It is formed by the evaporation of surface water, which leaves behind all dissolved solid impurities. When the water vapour condenses and falls as rain, it is essentially distilled water, although it may dissolve some atmospheric gases during its fall.

Answer: Rain water

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: For acid rain, the pH of rain water should be less than
questions.solution:
Normal rain water has a pH of about $5.6$ due to the dissolution of atmospheric carbon dioxide, which forms carbonic acid ($H_2CO_3$).

When the pH of rain water drops below $5.6$, it becomes more acidic than normal and is classified as acid rain.

Answer: 5.6

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following salts is responsible for temporary hardness of water?
questions.solution:
Temporary hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium, namely $Ca(HCO_3)_2$ and $Mg(HCO_3)_2$.

Permanent hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium.

Therefore, bicarbonates of magnesium are responsible for the temporary hardness of water.

Answer: Bicarbonates of magnesium

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is an endothermic reaction?
questions.solution:
Combustion of methane ($CH_4$) is an exothermic reaction as it releases heat.

The oxidation of glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) during respiration is an exothermic process that provides energy to living cells.

The synthesis of ammonia ($NH_3$) from nitrogen and hydrogen (Haber process) is an exothermic reaction.

The thermal decomposition of lead nitrate ($Pb(NO_3)_2$) requires heat to break down the reactant into simpler products ($PbO$, $NO_2$, and $O_2$). Since heat is absorbed, it is an endothermic reaction.

Answer: $2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \rightarrow 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following instruments can be used to measure −250°C temperature?
options: By using a mercury based thermometer
By using an alcohol based thermometer
questions.solution:
Mercury freezes at $-39^\circ\text{C}$, so a mercury-based thermometer cannot be used to measure $-250^\circ\text{C}$.

Alcohol freezes at $-115^\circ\text{C}$, so an alcohol-based thermometer is also unsuitable for measuring $-250^\circ\text{C}$.

A clinical thermometer is designed to measure human body temperature, typically in the narrow range of $35^\circ\text{C}$ to $42^\circ\text{C}$.

A thermocouple-based thermometer can measure a very wide range of temperatures, typically from $-270^\circ\text{C}$ to over $2000^\circ\text{C}$ depending on the metals used. Therefore, it can be used to measure $-250^\circ\text{C}$.

Answer: By using thermocouple based thermometer

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The quantity of heat needed to change unit mass of a substance from liquid to vapour without changing the temperature, is called
questions.solution:
The quantity of heat required to change the state of a unit mass of a substance from liquid to vapour at constant temperature is known as the specific latent heat of vaporization.

Specific heat is the heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass by one degree.

Thermal capacity is the heat required to raise the temperature of the entire body by one degree.

Therefore, the correct term is specific latent heat.

Answer: specific latent heat

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:
List I (Reaction)List II (Type)
A. $CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)$1. Single displacement
B. $CaCO_3(s) \rightarrow CaO(s) + CO_2(g)$2. Double displacement
C. $Pb(s) + CuCl_2(aq) \rightarrow PbCl_2(aq) + Cu(s)$3. Combination
D. $Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)$4. Decomposition
questions.solution:
Reaction A: $CaO(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2(aq)$ is a combination reaction because two substances combine to form a single product. (A → 3)

Reaction B: $CaCO_3(s) \rightarrow CaO(s) + CO_2(g)$ is a decomposition reaction because a single compound breaks down into two simpler substances upon heating. (B → 4)

Reaction C: $Pb(s) + CuCl_2(aq) \rightarrow PbCl_2(aq) + Cu(s)$ is a single displacement reaction because lead displaces copper from the copper chloride solution. (C → 1)

Reaction D: $Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)$ is a double displacement reaction because there is a mutual exchange of ions between the two reactants to form a precipitate. (D → 2)

The correct matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

Answer: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is known as 'water gas'?
questions.solution:
Water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide ($CO$) and hydrogen gas ($H_2$).

It is produced by passing steam over red-hot coke at high temperatures:

$C(s) + H_2O(g) \rightarrow CO(g) + H_2(g)$

This mixture is also known as synthesis gas or syngas.

Answer: $CO + H_2$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The optimum pH at which the enzymes pepsin and trypsin of the human alimentary canal works are
questions.solution:
Pepsin is a proteolytic enzyme secreted in the stomach, which requires a highly acidic medium for its optimal activity. The optimum pH for pepsin is around $1\cdot8$ to $2\cdot0$.

Trypsin is a proteolytic enzyme secreted by the pancreas into the small intestine, which requires a slightly alkaline medium for its optimal activity. The optimum pH for trypsin is around $7\cdot8$ to $8\cdot0$.

Therefore, the optimum pH values for pepsin and trypsin are approximately $2\cdot0$ and $7\cdot9$, respectively.

Answer: pH 2·0 and 7·9, respectively

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The amount of air breathed in and out during a normal respiration by human lungs is referred to as
questions.solution:
Tidal volume is the volume of air inspired or expired during a normal respiration. It is approximately $500$ mL for a healthy adult.

Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration.

Inspiratory reserve volume is the additional volume of air a person can inspire by a forcible inspiration.

Total lung capacity is the total volume of air accommodated in the lungs at the end of a forced inspiration.

Answer: Tidal volume

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The book 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection' was authored by
questions.solution:
The book 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection' was authored by Charles Darwin and published in 1859. It introduced the scientific theory that populations evolve over the course of generations through a process of natural selection.

Answer: Charles Darwin

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: For a material under static conditions, which one among the following statements is correct?
options: A perfect conductor can be charged
Both perfect conductor and insulator can be charged
Both perfect conductor and insulator cannot be charged
questions.solution:
Under static conditions, an insulator can be charged by methods such as friction or contact. The charge supplied to an insulator remains localized at the region of application because charges cannot move freely within the material.

A perfect conductor can also be charged. When a net charge is given to an isolated conductor, it redistributes itself entirely over its outer surface to maintain a zero electric field inside the material, which is a requirement for electrostatic equilibrium.

Therefore, both a perfect conductor and an insulator can be charged and hold a static charge.

Answer : Both perfect conductor and insulator can be charged

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following statements about arteries and veins in humans is NOT correct?
options: Arteries carry blood away from heart while veins bring blood towards the heart
Pulmonary arteries always carry oxygenated blood while Pulmonary veins always carry deoxygenated blood
Arteries have thicker and more elastic walls compared to veins in general
Arteries do not have valves but veins do have valves
questions.solution:
Arteries generally carry oxygenated blood away from the heart, but the pulmonary artery is an exception as it carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

Veins generally carry deoxygenated blood towards the heart, but the pulmonary vein is an exception as it carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

Therefore, the statement that pulmonary arteries always carry oxygenated blood and pulmonary veins always carry deoxygenated blood is incorrect.

Answer: Pulmonary arteries always carry oxygenated blood while Pulmonary veins always carry deoxygenated blood

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The menstrual cycle in females is controlled by hormones that are secreted by
questions.solution:
The menstrual cycle in females is regulated by the coordinated action of hormones from the hypothalamus, anterior pituitary gland, and ovaries.

The anterior pituitary gland secretes gonadotropins, namely Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH), which regulate the ovarian cycle.

The ovaries secrete the steroid hormones estrogen and progesterone, which regulate the uterine cycle and exert feedback control on the pituitary gland.

Lacrimal glands secrete tears, sebaceous glands secrete sebum, and the prostate gland is a part of the male reproductive system.

Answer: Ovary and pituitary gland

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Identify the functions that are controlled by the hind brain of human being
options: Involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation vomiting etc.
Controlling the regions receiving sensory impulses from receptors
Controlling the movement of voluntary muscles
Sensation of hunger or being full
questions.solution:
The hindbrain consists of the pons, cerebellum, and medulla.

The medulla oblongata controls various involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation, and vomiting.

The forebrain is responsible for receiving sensory impulses, controlling voluntary muscle movements, and contains the hypothalamus which controls the sensation of hunger and satiety.

Answer: Involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation vomiting etc.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Two conducting wires of the same material and of equal lengths and equal diameters are first connected in parallel and then in series in a circuit across the same potential difference. The ratio of heat produced in parallel and series combinations is
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of each wire be $R$.

When the wires are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is $R_p = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

When the wires are connected in series, the equivalent resistance is $R_s = 2R$.

The heat produced in a circuit across a potential difference $V$ in time $t$ is given by $H = \dfrac{V^2}{R_{eq}} t$.

The heat produced in the parallel combination is $H_p = \dfrac{V^2}{R_p} t = \dfrac{2V^2}{R} t$.

The heat produced in the series combination is $H_s = \dfrac{V^2}{R_s} t = \dfrac{V^2}{2R} t$.

The ratio of heat produced in parallel and series combinations is $\dfrac{H_p}{H_s} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2V^2}{R} t}{\dfrac{V^2}{2R} t} = 4$.

Thus, the required ratio is $4 : 1$.

Answer: 4 : 1

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following type of medicines is used for treating indigestion?
questions.solution:
Indigestion is typically caused by the overproduction of acid in the stomach.

Antacids are mild bases that are used to neutralize this excess acid and provide relief from indigestion.

Analgesics are used to relieve pain, antiseptics are applied to living tissues to prevent the growth of microbes, and antibiotics are used to treat bacterial infections.

Answer: Antacid

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which of the following organelles have their own DNA and ribosomes?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous cell organelles.

They possess their own circular, double-stranded DNA and 70S ribosomes, which allow them to synthesize some of their own proteins.

Other organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, cytoskeleton, and nucleolus do not contain their own DNA.

Answer: Mitochondria and Chloroplast

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Paragraph: The grouping or assemblage of plants, animals and microbes we observe when we study a natural forest, a grassland, a pond, a coral reef or some other undisturbed area, is referred to as the area's biota or biotic community. The plant portion of the biotic community includes all vegetation, from large trees down through to microscopic algae. Likewise, the animal portion includes everything from large mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians through to earthworms, tiny insects and mites. Microbes encompass a large array of microscopic bacteria, fungi and protozoans. Thus, the biotic community comprises a plant community, an animal community and a microbial community. The particular kind of biotic community found in a given area is, in large part, determined by abiotic factors such as the amount of water or moisture present, the temperature, the salinity, or the type of soil in the areThese abiotic factors both support and limit the particular community. For example, a relative lack of available moisture prevents the growth of most species of plants, but supports certain species, such as cacti; these kinds of areas are deserts. Land with plenty of available moisture and a suitable temperature supports forests. The presence of water is the major factor that sustains aquatic communities. The first step in investigating a biotic community may be simply to catalogue all the species present. Species are the different kinds of plants, animals and microbes in the community. A given species includes all those individuals which have a strong similarity in appearance to one another and which are distinct in appearance from other such groups. Each species in a biotic community is represented by a certain population - that is, by a certain number of individuals that make up the interbreeding, reproducing group.
Question: Which one of the following does not belong to the biotic community?
questions.solution: Water is an abiotic component that supports biotic communities but is not part of the biotic community itself. The biotic community consists of living organisms like humans, protozoa, and bushes (plants).

Land with plenty of available moisture and a suitable temperature supports forests. The presence of water is the major factor that sustains aquatic communities. The first step in investigating a biotic community may be simply to catalogue all the species present. Species are the different kinds of plants, animals and microbes in the community. A given species includes all those individuals which have a strong similarity in appearance to one another and which are distinct in appearance from other such groups. Each species in a biotic community is represented by a certain population - that is, by a certain number of individuals that make up the interbreeding, reproducing group.
Question: The nature of the biotic community largely depends on: 1. Biotic components 2. Abiotic components Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution: The passage states that the nature of the biotic community is largely determined by both biotic components (such as different kinds of plants, animals, and microbes) and abiotic components (such as water, temperature, salinity, and soil type).

Question: Which of the following is not an abiotic factor?

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: An infinite combination of resistors, each having resistance $R=4 \Omega$, is given below. What is the net resistance between the points A and B ? (Each resistance is of equal value, $R=4$ )
questions.solution:
Equivalent Resistance,
$\begin{array}{r}
y=\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{R} \| y \\
\Rightarrow y=\mathrm{R}+\frac{\mathrm{R} \times y}{\mathrm{R}+y} \\
\Rightarrow y=\frac{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{R} y+\mathrm{R} y}{\mathrm{R}+y} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{R} y+y^2=\mathrm{R}^2+2 \mathrm{R} y \\
\Rightarrow y^2-4 y-16=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}} \text { or } y=2+2 \sqrt{5} \text { ohm }
\end{array}$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which of the following forces is/are fundamental in nature?
1. Gravitational force
2. Electromagnetic forces
3. Strong and weak nuclear forces
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
1. Gravitational force: This force is fundamental in nature and acts universally between all objects with mass. It governs the motions of planets, stars, and galaxies.
2. Electromagnetic force: This force is also fundamental and governs the interactions between electrically charged particles. It includes forces like attraction between opposite charges (electrostatic force) and interactions involving magnetic fields.
3. Strong and weak nuclear forces: These are fundamental forces that operate at the level of subatomic particles within atomic nuclei. Strong nuclear force: It binds protons and neutrons together in atomic nuclei. Weak nuclear force: It governs processes such as radioactive decay.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A spherical shell of outer radius $R$ and inner radius $\mathrm{R} / 2$ contains a solid sphere of radius $\mathrm{R} / 2$ (see figure). The density of the material of the solid sphere is $\rho$ and that of the shell is $\rho / 2$. What is the average mass density of the larger sphere thus formed?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Average density }=\frac{\text { Total mass }}{\text { Total volume }} \\
& =\frac{\rho_1 V_1+\rho_2 V_2}{V} \\
& =\frac{\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\right)^3+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3-\frac{4}{3} \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{2}\right)^3\right]}{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3} \\
& =\frac{\rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi \frac{\mathrm{R}^3}{8}+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3-\frac{4}{3} \pi \frac{\mathrm{R}^3}{8}\right]}{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3} \\
& =\frac{\rho}{8}+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[1-\frac{1}{8}\right] \\
& =\frac{\rho}{8}+\frac{\rho}{2}\left[\frac{7}{8}\right] \\
& =\frac{\rho}{8}+\frac{7 \rho}{16} \\
& =\frac{2 \rho+7 \rho}{16}=\frac{9 \rho}{16} .
\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Formula used,
Average atomic mass
$=\frac{\Sigma \% ~\text { abundance } \times \text { atomic mass }}{\Sigma \text { total abundance }}\begin{aligned}
\text { Let, } \quad \% ~\text { of } \mathrm{B}^{10} & =x \\
\% ~\text { of } \mathrm{B}^{11} & =100-x \\
\text { average atomic mass } & =10.81 \\
10.81 & =\frac{x \times 10+(100-x) \times 11}{100} \\
1081 & =10 x+1100-11 x \\
-19 & =-x \\
x & =19 \\
\% ~\text { of } \mathrm{B}^{10} & =19 \% ~\\
\% ~\text { of } \mathrm{B}^{11} & =81 \%
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Diamond is hard due to extended covalent bonding in it
Fullerene is composed of five and six membered rings
Diamond is a good conductor of electricity
Graphite is used as a lubricant
questions.solution:
In diamond, each carbon atom is $sp^3$ hybridized and covalently bonded to four other carbon atoms, forming a rigid three-dimensional network. Since all four valence electrons of each carbon atom are localized in these strong covalent bonds, there are no free electrons available to conduct electricity. Thus, diamond is an insulator, not a good conductor of electricity.

The other statements are correct:
Diamond is extremely hard due to its extended three-dimensional covalent bonding.
Fullerenes (like $C_{60}$) are composed of both five-membered and six-membered carbon rings.
Graphite has a layered structure with weak van der Waals forces between the layers, allowing them to slide over one another, making it an excellent solid lubricant.

Answer: Diamond is a good conductor of electricity

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The human eye is like a camera that has a lens with:
options: fixed focal length and fixed asperture size.
variable focal length and fixed aperture size.
fixed focal length and variable aperture size.
variable focal length and variable aperture size.
questions.solution: Variable focal length and variable aperture size: This option means that both the focal length and the aperture size can change. The human eye indeed has a variable focal length (accommodation allows it to focus on objects at varying distances) and a variable aperture size (pupil dilation adjusts based on light conditions).

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which among the following are essential constituents of Portland cement?
questions.solution:
Portland cement, which is the most common type of cement used in construction, is composed primarily of the following essential constituents:
- Silica (Silicon dioxide): Provides strength to the cement and contributes to its early strength development.
- Alumina (Aluminium oxide): Helps in quick setting and hardening of cement.
- Lime (Calcium oxide or calcium hydroxide): Acts as a binding material and contributes to the strength and durability of the cement.

questions.solution:
The oxidation state of vanadium in

The oxidation state of O -atom is -2 .

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists:
$\begin{array}{ll}\begin{array}{c} \text{List-I} \\ \text{(Allotrope of Carbon)} \end{array} & \begin{array}{c} \text{List-II} \\ \text{(Property)} \end{array} \\ \text{(a) Graphite} & \begin{array}{l} \text{(i) } \text{Thinnest and strongest} \\ \text{material} \end{array} \\ \text{(b) Diamond} & \begin{array}{l} \text{(ii) } \text{Hardest natural substance} \end{array} \\ \text{(c) Fullerene} & \begin{array}{l} \text{(iii) } \text{Very light and strong} \\ \text{material} \end{array} \\ \text{(d) Graphene} & \begin{array}{l} \text{(iv) } \text{Soft and slippery material} \end{array} \end{array}$
questions.solution:
(a) Graphite (iv) Soft and slippery material: Graphite is composed of layers of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice. These layers are weakly bonded together, allowing them to slide over each other easily. This gives graphite its characteristic soft and slippery feel, making it suitable as a lubricant and in pencils.
(b) Diamond (ii) Hardest natural substance: Diamond is made up of carbon atoms arranged in a tetrahedral lattice structure, forming a very strong covalent bond network. This structure gives diamond its exceptional hardness, making it the hardest natural substance known.
(c) Fullerene (iii) Very light and strong material: Fullerene molecules, such as Buckminsterfullerene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{60}\right)$, are spherical carbon molecules with a unique structure. They are lightweight due to their hollow structure and have remarkable strength, despite their lightness.
(d) Graphene (i) Thinnest and strongest material: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice. It is incredibly thin, with a thickness of just one atom. Despite its thinness, graphene is exceptionally strong, with a tensile strength much higher than steel.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding animal cell membrane is correct?
options: They are composed of phospholipids only.
They are composed of proteins only.
They are composed of phospholipids and proteins only.
They are composed of phospholipids, proteins and cholesterol (lipid).
questions.solution: The cell membrane of animal cells is primarily composed of phospholipids, which form a bilayer structure. Embedded within or attached to this phospholipid bilayer are proteins that serve various functions like transport and signaling. Additionally, cholesterol molecules are interspersed among the phospholipids, contributing to the membrane's stability and fluidity. This composition of phospholipids, proteins, and cholesterol allows the cell membrane to regulate the passage of molecules and ions, maintain cell shape, and facilitate communication with the external environment, making it crucial for the cell's survival and function.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Iodized salt is a vital part of our diet as it is essential for the synthesis of
questions.solution:
Iodine is an essential trace element required by the thyroid gland to synthesize thyroid hormones, primarily thyroxin (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).

Deficiency of iodine in the diet leads to decreased production of thyroxin, which can cause conditions like goiter and hypothyroidism.

Therefore, iodized salt is a vital part of our diet as it provides the necessary iodine for the synthesis of thyroxin.

Answer: Thyroxin

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which of the following is not a part of compounds microscope?
questions.solution: A compound microscope typically consists of several parts including a mirror or light source (to illuminate the specimen), a stage (where the specimen is placed), clips (to hold the specimen slide in place), objective lenses (to magnify the specimen), an eyepiece or ocular lens (through which the observer views the specimen), and focusing knobs (to bring the specimen into sharp focus). The retina, however, is a part of the eye and not a component of the compound microscope.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following blood cells type secrete large number of antibodies during an immune response of the body?
questions.solution:
Antibodies are proteinaceous molecules produced by B-lymphocytes in response to pathogens. B-lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells, which secrete a large number of antibodies into the blood to fight infections.

Neutrophils and monocytes are phagocytic cells that engulf and destroy foreign organisms.

Eosinophils are associated with allergic reactions and immunity against certain parasites.

Therefore, lymphocytes are the blood cells that secrete antibodies during an immune response.

Answer: Lymphocytes

Storage and regulated release of bile
Secretion of lipase, amylase and protease
questions.solution: The pancreas secretes enzymes such as lipase (to digest fats), amylase (to digest carbohydrates), and protease (to digest proteins) into the small intestine. These enzymes play a crucial role in breaking down food components so that they can be absorbed and utilized by the body.

- Monocyte: A type of white blood cell involved in immune response.
- Chondrocyte: Cartilage cells found in connective tissue.
- Basophil: A type of white blood cell involved in allergic reactions and inflammation.
- Lymphocyte: White blood cells crucial for immune defense.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. DNA replication takes place when chromatin is opened up.
2. Chromatin organises itself into rod-shaped chromosomes before cell division.
3. Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes have the same process for cell division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1. DNA replication does indeed take place when chromatin (the complex of DNA and proteins) is opened up. During replication, the chromatin structure unfolds to allow access to the DNA strands so that they can be copied.
2. Before cell division, chromatin condenses and organizes itself into rod-shaped structures called chromosomes. This condensation ensures that each daughter cell receives a complete set of genetic information during cell division.

questions.solution:

- Tissue: Tissues are groups of cells that work together to perform a specific function.
- Organ: Organs are structures composed of different tissues working together to perform a complex function.
- Organism: An organism is a living being composed of various organ systems working together.

As the scale is in equilibrium, net torque must be zero,
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{N}_1 d_1-\mathrm{N}_2 d_2 & =0 \\
\mathrm{~N}_1 \times 0.3 & =\mathrm{N}_2 \times 0.1 \\
3 \mathrm{~N}_1 & =\mathrm{N}_2

Also, force must be balance,
$\begin{aligned}

\mathrm{N}_1+3 \mathrm{~N}_2 & =0.24 \times 10 \\
4 \mathrm{~N}_1 & =2.4 \\
\mathrm{~N}_1 & =0.6 \mathrm{~N} \\
\mathrm{~N}_2 & =3 \mathrm{~N}_1=3 \times 0.6=1.8 \mathrm{~N}

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Escape speed from the Earth is close to $11.2 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. On another planet whose radius is half of the Earth's radius and whose mass density is four times that of the Earth, the escape speed in $\mathrm{km} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ will be close to:
questions.solution:
Escape velocity is given by,
$\begin{array}{rlrl}
\Rightarrow & v & =\sqrt{2 g \mathrm{R}} \\
\Rightarrow & v & =\sqrt{2 \frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}^2} \times \mathrm{R}}=\sqrt{2 \frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}}} \\
& \text { Also, } & v & =\sqrt{2 \mathrm{G} \times \rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^2}=11.2 \\
& & v^{\prime} & =\sqrt{2 \mathrm{G} \times 4 \rho \times \frac{4}{3} \pi \frac{\mathrm{R}^2}{4}}=11.2
\end{array}$
Hence, escape velocity remains same.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following about different frictional force is correct?
options: Kinetic fricition > Static friction > Rolling friction
Static friction > Rolling fricition > Kinetic fricition
Static friction > Kinetic friction > Rolling friction
Static friction > Kinetic friction $=$ Rolling friction
questions.solution:
Static friction > Kinetic friction > Rolling friction
- Static friction is the frictional force that prevents two surfaces from sliding past each other when they are not moving relative to each other.
- Kinetic friction is the frictional force that opposes the relative motion of two surfaces sliding past each other.
- Rolling friction is the frictional force that opposes the motion of a rolling object.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following does not apply to sound waves in fluids?
options: They need a medium to travel
They travel faster in liquids than in gases
questions.solution: Sound waves in fluids (liquids and gases) are longitudinal waves, not transverse. This means the vibrations occur in the same direction as the wave's propagation. Sound waves do transport energy and require a medium to travel because they propagate through the vibration of particles in the medium. The speed of sound generally increases in liquids compared to gases because liquids are denser and transmit sound more effectively.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Which one of the following statements regarding simple pendulum is correct?
Simple pendulum has a time period independent of amplitude:
options: only for small amplitudes because then the net force on its bob is independent of its displacement.
for any amplitude because the net force on the bob is always proportional to its displacement.
for any amplitude because the net force on the bob is independent of its displacement.
only for small amplitudes because then the net force on its bob is proportional to its displacement.
questions.solution:
We have,
$\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}, \text { also } \mathrm{F}=-k x$
For small amplitudes the restoring force on the pendulum bob is directly proportional to its displacement. This leads to simple harmonic motion, where the time period is independent of the amplitude. For larger amplitude the restoring force is no longer directly proportional to displacement, Consequently the time period slightly dependent on the amplitude.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Water gas is a mixture of:
questions.solution:
Water gas is a mixture of carbon monoxide $(\mathrm{CO})$ and hydrogen $\left(\mathrm{H}_2\right)$, typically produced through a process known as gasification. In this process, steam $\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right.$ ) is passed over red-hot coke (a form of carbon), which results in the following endothermic reaction:
$\mathrm{C}(\text { coke })+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \text { (steam) } \rightarrow \mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{H}_2$
This reaction occurs at high temperatures and requires continuous heating to maintain the reaction. The resulting water gas, composed of CO and $\mathrm{H}_2$, can be used as a fuel or as an intermediate in the production of other chemicals. It is an important industrial process for generating a synthesis gas that can be used in various applications, including the synthesis of methanol and hydrocarbons via the Fischer-Tropsch process.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following compounds has a sweet and fruity smell?
questions.solution: Ethyl acetate, known for its sweet and fruity smell, is commonly used in perfumes and flavorings. This ester is responsible for the pleasant aromas found in many fruits and is often utilized in the food and beverage industry to enhance flavors. Unlike ethyl alcohol, which has an alcoholic smell, and acetic acid, which has a sharp vinegar-like odor, ethyl acetate provides a distinctly sweet fragrance that is easily recognizable.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: What is the coordination number of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ ions in NaCl lattice?
questions.solution: In the NaCl (sodium chloride) crystal lattice, each sodium ion $\left(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\right)$is surrounded by 6 chloride ions ( $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$), and each chloride ion is surrounded by 6 sodium ions. This arrangement is known as a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, where each ion is in contact with 6 nearest neighbours in all directions. This high coordination number of 6 ensures strong electrostatic interactions between ions, contributing to the stability of the crystal lattice and the characteristic properties of NaCl .

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one among the following is known as Milk of Magnesia?
questions.solution: Milk of Magnesia refers to a suspension of magnesium hydroxide in water, known for its medicinal use as an antacid and laxative. When ingested, it neutralizes stomach acid and provides relief from indigestion and heartburn due to its alkaline nature. It also acts as a mild laxative by drawing water into the intestines, thereby promoting bowel movements.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Soap with water forms:
questions.solution: When soap is mixed with water, it forms a lyotropic liquid crystal. Lyotropic liquid crystals are formed by amphiphilic molecules (such as soap molecules) in solution. These molecules have both hydrophilic (water-attracting) and hydrophobic (waterrepelling) parts. In the presence of water, soap molecules self-organize into structures where the hydrophobic parts cluster together and the hydrophilic parts interact with water molecules.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Litmus, a well-known acid-base indicator, is derived from:
questions.solution: Litmus, a natural dye used as an acid-base indicator, is derived from lichens. Lichens are symbiotic organisms composed of a fungus (usually an ascomycete) and an algae or cyanobacterium. questions.q: A ball of 0.1 kg mass is dropped on a hard floor from a height of 0.45 m and rises to a height of 0.20 m . If it was in touch with the floor for 0.1 s , the net force it applied on the floor while bouncing is: (take the gravitational acceleration $g=10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution:
As per conservation of energy,
$\frac{1}{2} m u^2=m g h\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad u & =\sqrt{2 g h} \\
& =\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.45} \\
& =\sqrt{9}=3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
After rebound some of its kinetic energy gets lost and remaining gets converted into Potential energy
Hence, $\quad \frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g h^{\prime}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad v & =\sqrt{2 g h^{\prime}} \\
& =\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.20} \\
& =\sqrt{4}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
We know that, $\mathrm{F}=\frac{m v-m u}{t}=\frac{m(v-u)}{t}$
Taking sign consideration
$\mathrm{F}=\frac{0.1(-2-3)}{0.1}=-5 \mathrm{~N} .$
(-ve sign indicated retarding force)

questions.solution: Latent heat of fusion of water is very low: This is incorrect. Water actually has a high latent heat of fusion, which is the amount of heat required to convert ice at its melting point into water without changing its temperature. options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement-2 is the correct explanation of Statement-1.
Both the statements are individually true, but Statement-2 is not the correct explanation of Statement-1.
Statement-1 is true, but Statement-2 is false.
Statement-2 is true, but Statement-1 is false.
questions.solution: Infrared waves, also known as heat waves, are a type of electromagnetic radiation emitted by objects due to their temperature. Water molecules effectively absorb infrared waves, primarily through their vibrational modes, which results in the molecules gaining energy and contributing to heat. While it's accurate to call infrared waves "heat waves" due to their heating effect when absorbed by substances, this terminology doesn't solely stem from water's absorption behaviour. Therefore, both statements are individually correct. However, the absorption by water doesn't directly explain why infrared waves are termed heat waves in general usage.

questions.q: A bullet of mass 10 g is horizontally fired with velocity $300 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ from a pistol of mass 1 kg . What is the recoil velocity of the pistol?
questions.solution:
When a bullet is fired by the gun and gun moves in backword direction with a particular speed known as recoil velocity of the gun.
Let $m$ and $M$ be the masses of bullet and gun, respectively. If $v$ and $V$ are the velocities of the bullet and gun, respectively after the firing then:-
$0=\mathrm{mv}+\mathrm{MV}$
Therefore $\mathrm{V}=-(\mathrm{mv} / \mathrm{M})$
Putting the values, $V=-(0.01 \mathrm{~kg}$ X $300 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}) /(1 \mathrm{Kg})$
The recoil velocity of gun $=-\mathrm{3 ~ m} / \mathrm{s}$
The negative sign indicates that the gun moves in a direction to that of the bullet.

questions.q: Chlorine occurs in nature in two isotopic forms of masses 35 u and 37 u in the ratio of $3: 1$ respectively. What is the average atomic mass of the Chlorine atom?
questions.solution:
The isotopes of chlorine are in the ratio $3: 1$.
Therefore, in any sample of chlorine, ${ }_{17}^{35} \mathrm{CI}$ will constitute $75 \%$ and ${ }_{17}^{35} \mathrm{CI}$ will constitute $25 \%$.
The proportion in which the isotopes are found in nature is always constant.
Therefore, in a sample of chlorine, the average atomic mass would be,
The average atomic mass of chlorine
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{35 \times 75}{100}\right)+\left(\frac{37 \times 25}{100}\right) \\
& =\frac{105}{4}+\frac{37}{4}=\frac{142}{4} \\
& =35.5 \mathrm{u}
\end{aligned}$
The average atomic mass of chlorine is equal to 35.5 u .

questions.solution:

questions.q: Power of lens of focal length 25 cm is
questions.solution:
We define the power of a lens as the reciprocal of the focal length of the lens. So, the power of the lens is expressed as $\mathrm{P}=1 / \mathrm{f}$
Where $f$ is the focal length and is expressed in meters. So, the unit of power of the lens is expressed in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. This is also expressed as diopter.
As we know that the focal length of a convex lens is taken as in positive sign and the focal length of a concave lens is taken negatively. So, the power of a convex lens is positive, and the power of a concave lens is negative.
In this question, it is given that the lens is convex, and its focal length is 25 cm . First, we will convert the focal length into meters.
$\Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{~cm}=0.25 \mathrm{~m} \Rightarrow 25 \mathrm{~cm}=0.25 \mathrm{~m}$
Now, substituting the value of focal length in the formula of power of lens we get
$\begin{aligned}
& P=\frac{1}{0.25} \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \\
& \Rightarrow P=4 \mathrm{~m}^{-1}
\end{aligned}\mathrm{m}-1$ is also expressed as diopters or $D$
As it is a convex lens so its power is positive.
Thus, the power of the lens is +4 D .

By 1920, physicists knew that most of the mass of the atom was located in a nucleus at its center, and that this central core contained protons. In May 1932 James Chadwick announced that the core also contained a new uncharged particle, which he called the neutron.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The statement "friction force is a contact force while magnetic force is a non-contact force" is
options: either true or false depending upon the temperature of the surroundings.
questions.solution:
Magnetic forces are non- contact forces; they pull or push on objects without touching them. Magnets are only attracted to a few 'magnetic' metals and not all matter. Magnets are attracted to and repel other magnet. Non-contact force occurs due to either attraction or repulsion between two objects such that there is no contact between these objects. There is no field linked with the contact force. There is always a field linked with non-contact force.
- Friction is a contact force when two surfaces interact. The static friction case is similar for when the two surfaces are stationary relative to each other. In static friction, the frictional force is whatever value it needs to be to prevent sliding up to some maximum value.

options: real and thus can be photographed.
virtual and nearer than the object.
questions.solution:
The image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual (meaning that the light rays do not actually come from the image), upright, and of the same shape and size as the object it is reflecting. A virtual image is a copy of an object formed at the location from which the light rays appear to come.
An image formed by a plane mirror has the following characteristics: $\square$
- Virtual and erect.
- Behind the mirror.
- The size of the image is equal to the size of the object.
- Laterally inverted image (image of the left side visible on the right side).

options: Light travels at different speeds in different media.
Light travels at almost 300 million metres per second in air.
Light speeds down as it leaves a water surface and enters the air.
Light speeds up as it leaves a glass surface and enters the air.
questions.solution:
A light ray is a line (straight or curved) that is perpendicular to the light's wavefronts; its tangent is collinear with the wave vector. Light rays in homogeneous media are straight. They bend at the interface between two dissimilar media and may be curved in a medium in which the refractive index changes
Light waves travel fastest through a vacuum and air, and slower through other materials such as glass or water. Light travels at approximately 300,000 kilometers per second in a vacuum, which has a refractive index of 1.0 , but it slows down to 225,000 kilometers per second in water and 200,000 kilometers per second in glass.

Rayleigh scattering law. It simply states that :

More the index more will be the deviation

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following conclusions could not be derived from Rutherford's $\alpha$-particle scattering experiment?
options: Most of the space in the atom is empty.
The radius of the atom is about $10^5$ times the radius of the nucleus.
Electrons move in a circular path of fixed energy called orbits.
Nearly all the mass of the atom resides in the nucleus.
questions.solution:
Conclusion of Rutherford's scattering experiment: Most of the space inside the atom is empty because most of the $\alpha$-particles passed through the gold foil without getting deflected.
- Very few particles were deflected from their path, indicating that the positive charge of the atom occupies very little space.
- A very small fraction of $\alpha$-particles were deflected by very large angles, indicating that all the positive charge and mass of the gold atom were concentrated in a very small volume within the atom.
- From the data he also calculated that the radius of the nucleus is about $10^5$ times less than the radius of the atom.

options: reflection of starlight from the oceanic surface.
questions.solution:
- The twinkling of a star is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight. The starlight, on entering the earth's atmosphere, undergoes refraction continuously before it reaches the earth.
- As light from a star races through our atmosphere, it bounces and bumps through the different layers, bending the light before you see it. Since the hot and cold layers of air keep moving, the bending of the light changes too, which causes the star's appearance to wobble or twinkle.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Transformation of meristematic cells into specific permanent tissues occurs by the process of
questions.solution:
- The permanent tissues always differentiate from the meristematic cells, during the process of growth. These meristematic cells lose the ability to divide and take up a specific role. This process of taking up a permanent shape, size and a function is called cellular differentiation.
- The cells derived from root apical and shoot-apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions.
- This act leading to maturation is termed as differentiation. During differentiation, cells undergo few to major structural changes both in their cell walls and protoplasm.
- The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation.
- For example, formation of meristems - interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells. While doing so, such meristems / tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform specific functions, i.e., get redifferentiated.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Two equal resistors R are connected in parallel, and a battery of 12 V is connected across this combination. A dc current of 100 mA flows through the circuit as shown below:
The value of $R$ is
questions.solution:
Let R' be the equivalent resistance of two resistors.
As they are connected in parallel
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{R}+\frac{1}{R} \\
& R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2} (i)
\end{aligned}$
Using ohm's law
$V=I R^{\prime}\begin{aligned}
& R^{\prime}=\frac{V}{I}=\frac{12}{100 \times 10^{-3}} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}^{\prime}=120 \Omega
\end{aligned}$
But, $R^{\prime}=\frac{R}{2}\therefore \quad \mathrm{R}=2 \times \mathrm{R}^{\prime}=2 \times 120=240 \Omega$

questions.q: Two planets orbit the Sun in circular orbits, with their radius of orbit as $R_1=R$ and $R_2=4 R$. Ratio of their periods $\left(\mathrm{T}_1 / \mathrm{T}_2\right)$ around the Sun will be
questions.solution:
According to Kepler's law of planetary motion, $\mathrm{T}^2 \propto \mathrm{R}^3$
Therefore, the ratio of the time period is given by,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{T_1^2}{T_2^2}=\frac{R^3}{(4 R)^3}=\frac{1}{64} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{T_1}{T_2}=\frac{1}{8}
\end{aligned}$
i.e., $T_1: T_2$ is $1: 8$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about sound is NOT correct?
options: Sound travels at a speed slower than the speed of light
Sound travels faster in moist air than in dry air
questions.solution:
The sensation felt by our ears is called sound. It is a form of energy which makes us hear. Sound travels in the form of wave.
Longitudinal Waves: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth in the 'same direction' in which the wave is moving. Medium can be solid, liquid or gases. Therefore, sound waves are longitudinal waves. Sound is a longitudinal wave which consists of compressions and rarefactions travelling through a medium.
Transverse Waves: A wave in which the particles of the medium vibrate up and down 'at right angles' to the direction in which the wave is moving. These waves are produced only in a solids and liquids but not in gases.

questions.q: A lens has a power of +2.0 Dioptre. Which one of the following statements about the lens is true?
options: The lens is concave and has a focal length of 0.5 metre
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 2.0 metre
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 0.5 metre
The lens is concave and has a focal length of 2.0 metre
questions.solution:
A dioptre, is a unit of measurement of the optical power of a lens, which is equal to the reciprocal of the focal length measured in meters (that is, $1 / \mathrm{f}$ metres). It is thus a unit of reciprocal length.
Hence, $\mathrm{P}=1 / \mathrm{f} \Rightarrow 2=1 / \mathrm{f} \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=0.5$ meter.
As the value is positive, it is a positive lens, that is, convex. Hence, the option (c) is true.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT the unit of energy?
questions.solution:
A watt-hour $(\mathrm{Wh})$ is a unit of energy; it's a way to measure the amount of work performed or generated. Household appliances and other electrical devices perform "work" and that requires energy in the form of electricity. The joule (symbol J) is the SI unit of energy-a measure of the capacity to do work or generate heat. Newton-Meter $(\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m})$ is a unit of energy. One joule equals the work done (or energy expended) by a force of one newton (N) acting over a distance of one meter (m).
SI unit for force is Newton (N).
$1 \mathrm{~N}=1 \mathrm{~kg} \cdot \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
Thus, $\mathrm{kg} \cdot \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ is the unit of Force not energy.

$\mathrm{C}=$ Speed of light

Thus, Force becomes half.

options: A convex lens produces both real and virtual images
A concave lens produces both real and virtual images.
A convex lens can produce images equal, greater and smaller than the size of the object.
A concave lens always produces images smaller than the size of the object.
questions.solution: Concave lenses refract parallel light waves, causing them to disperse. The three light rays traveling into the concave lens shown above travel away from each other. For this reason, concave lens are also called diverging lenses. As a result of this light divergence, concave lenses create only virtual images.
