questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is termed as 'Dry ice'?
questions.solution: Dry Ice is the common name for solid carbon dioxide (CO2). Carbon dioxide typically exists as a gas at room temperature, but can also be frozen at very cold temperatures to form a solid known as dry ice.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about diamond and graphite is not correct?
options: Diamond has tetrahedral structure, whereas graphite has a hexagonal planar structure.
Both physical and chemical properties of diamond and graphite are different.
Graphite is soft but diamond is hard.
Graphite is a good conductor of electricity while diamond is not.
questions.solution: Since they are both made of carbon their chemical properties are the same. Graphite has a layered sheet-like structure with each layer consisting of hexagonal rings, this is because all carbon atoms are sp2 hybridised. Diamond has a tetrahedral structure since all carbon atoms are sp 3 hybridised.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Blood is a type of
questions.solution: Blood is considered a connective tissue because it has a matrix. It contains different cells like RBCs, WBCs, thrombocytes in addition to various other components like proteins and plasma.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about water is not true?
options: Hydrogen bonds are present in liquid water
Water has a high boiling point
Water has a high heat of fusion
Water is a non polar molecule
questions.solution: Water $\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)$ is a polar molecule due to uneven distribution of electron density. Water has a partial negative charge near the oxygen atom due the unshared pairs of electrons, and partial positive charges near the hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Mitochondria are able to produce their own
questions.solution:
Mitochondria is a double-membrane-bound organelle found in most eukaryotic organisms.
These organelles are able to make their own proteins because they have their own ribosomes and DNA.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
Flexibility in plants is due to selerenchyma.
Xylem consists of sieve plate sieve tube and companion cells.
questions.solution: A tissue in vascular plants that carries water and dissolved minerals from the roots and provides support for softer tissues. Xylem consists of several different types of cells: fibers for support, parenchyma for storage, and tracheary elements for the transport of water.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Water is heated with a coil of resistance R connected to domestic supply. The rise of temperature of water will depend on
1. Supply voltage
2. Current passing through the coil.
3. Time for which voltage is supplied.
Select the correct answer from among the following:
questions.solution: The heating effect generated inside a conductor depends upon the resistance of the conductor, the time, $t$ for which current flows and the current itself.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: In an incandescent electric bulb, the filament of the bulb is made up of which metal?
questions.solution: The filament is the part of the light bulb that produces light. Filaments in incandescent light bulbs are made of tungsten. Whenever an electric current goes through the filament, the filament glows. The reason tungsten is used is because it has the highest melting temperature of any element at 3600 K . For a typical incandescent light bulb, the Tungsten filament operates at approximately 2500 Celsius. Hence, the filaments are made of tungsten.

questions.solution: T is inversely proportional to sqrt (g) and independent on mass, hence in this case it will be sqrt (2) T .

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding cathode rays is not correct?
options: Cathode ray particles start from anode and move towards cathode.
In the absence of electrical and magnetic fields, cathode rays travel in straight lines.
Television picture tubes are cathode ray tubes.
questions.solution: Cathode are produced by the negative electrode, or cathode, in an evacuated tube, and travel towards the anode. They travel in straight lines and cast sharp shadows. They have energy and can do work. They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields and have a negative charge.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: A very large volume of hydrogen can be accommodated by making
questions.solution: Hydrides, hydrogen occupies interstices in the metal lattice producing distortion without any change in its type. Consequently, they were termed as interstitial hydrides. Some of the metals (e.g., Pd, Pt) can accommodate a very large volume of hydrogen and, therefore, can be used as its storage media. This property has high potential for hydrogen storage and as a source of energy.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is not a monatomic element?
questions.solution: Monoatomic elements are simply elements that are stable as single atoms Examples of monatomic elements includeare the noble gases, such as: Helium etc. The elements hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine occur naturally as the diatomic molecules of their atoms.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: The electron releasing tendency of the metals, zinc, copper and silver. Zinc has higher oxidation potential than copper, copper has higher oxidation potential than silver.

questions.solution: Thyroxine is the main hormone secreted into the bloodstream by the thyroid gland. Thyroid hormones play vital roles in regulating the body's metabolic rate (BMR) including muscle control, brain and maintenance of bones.

questions.solution: Salmonella typhi is the causative agent of typhoid fever. It is a gram-negative, shaped bacterium, which is spread through feces, causes intestinal hemorrhage, high fever, delirium and dehydration.

options: Viruses need living cells to reproduce.
Viruses can synthesize their food through photosynthesis.
Viruses are similar to chemical substances outside the host.
questions.solution: A virus is a small infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism. Viruses can infect all types of life forms, from animals and plants to microorganisms.

questions.solution: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of vitamin C, or ascorbic acid. The deficiency leads to symptoms of weakness, anemia, gum disease, and skin problems as vitamin C is needed for making collagen, an important component of connective tissues.

questions.solution: Marsilea is a genus of approximately 65 species of aquatic ferns of the family Marsileaceae. Marsilea has vascular tissue. The species of Marsilea are generally aquatic or amphibious in nature with their roots embedded in mud or damp soil.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following energy is stored in the links between the atoms?
questions.solution: Chemical energy is stored in the links between the atoms. Chemical energy may be released during a chemical reaction, often in the form of heat; such reactions are called exothermic. Batteries, biomass, petroleum, natural gas, and coal are examples of stored chemical energy.

Panchanan Maheshwari popularized the use of embryological character in taxonomy. Due to his important contributions in this field he is regarded as father of Indian Plant embryology.
Embryology is the study of micro- and mega-sporogenesis, gametophyte development, fertilization, and development of endosperm. embryo. and seed coats.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a synthetic detergent?
questions.solution: A synthetic detergent is the sodium salt of sulphonic acid which has cleansing properties in water. It consists of a long hydrocarbon chain which is hydrophobic and a short ionic part which is hydrophilic. Examples: (i) Sodium lauryl sulphate and (ii) Sodium n-dodecyl sulphate.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The loudness of sound depends upon the
options: velocity of sound waves in the medium.
frequency and velocity of the sound waves.
questions.solution: The loudness of a sound depends upon the amplitude. Loudness of a sound depends on the amplitude of the vibration producing that sound. Greater is the amplitude of vibration, louder is the sound produced by it.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following metals does NOT react with cold water?
questions.solution: Magnesium is a chemical element with the symbol Mg. Magnesium is the ninth most abundant element in the universe. Its use as a structural material is limited since it burns at relatively low temperatures. Magnesium is frequently alloyed with aluminum, which makes aluminum easier to roll, extrude and weld.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Light rays move in straight lines. But through an optical fibre, they can move in any type of zigzag path because.
options: the holes through the fibre are extremely fine.
light rays are absorbed at the entry end and relieved at the exit end of the fibre.
scattering of light occurs inside the fibre.
successive total internal reflections occur as a ray moves through the fibre.
questions.solution: An optical fiber transmit data in the form of light particles that pulse through a fiber optic cable. The glass fiber core and the cladding each have a different refractive index that bends incoming light at a certain angle. When light signals are sent through the fiber optic cable, they reflect off the core and cladding in a series of zig-zag bounces, adhering to a process called total internal reflection.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of a clean fuel?

It produces less pollution than the alternatives and it is used as a substitute for fossil fuels. Examples of clean fuels include most types of ethanol, biodiesel, natural gas, biogas, electricity, propane and hydrogen.

questions.solution: Isoelectronic refers to two atoms, ions or molecules that have the same electronic structure and the same number of valence electrons. Isoelectronic ions are ions that have the same number of electrons. There are many ions that are isoelectronic. Examples of Isoelectronic Ions and Elements: $\mathrm{He}, \mathrm{Li}^{+}, \mathrm{He}, \mathrm{Be}^{2+}, \mathrm{Ar}, \mathrm{S}^2-, \mathrm{Na}^{+}, \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following can charge an insulator?
questions.solution: Insulator can be charged by methods of friction and induction. Charge stored in this process will be static.

questions.subject: General Ability

questions.solution: Biogas is primarily composed of methane and carbon dioxide ( 45 to $70 \%$ methane 30 to $45 \%$ carbon dioxide.). It also contains trace amounts of nitrogen, hydrogen, and carbon monoxide.

options: The solution turns green in colour after the reaction

As you can see, copper does not displace iron from its solution since it is less reactive than iron. A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its solution.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is an organic acid?
questions.solution:
Organic acid is a type of organic compound that typically has acidic properties. A common example of organic acids are called carboxyl acids, which are generally known as weak acids and do not totally dissociate in a medium such as water, unlike with strong minerals.
The simplest form of organic acids, such as acetic and formic, are typically used in stimulation treatments against corrosion for gas and oil, since these are less reactive compared to hydrochloric acid and other strong acids.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Who among the following has explained the phenomenon of photoelectric effect?
questions.solution: Albert Einstein explained the phenomenon of photoelectric effect. The photoelectric effect is a phenomenon where electrons are emitted from the metal surface when the light of sufficient frequency is incident upon.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: The equivalent weight of oxalic acid in $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is
questions.solution:
The equivalent weight of oxalic acid in $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is 63.
- The molecular weight of oxalic acid $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)$ is 90.
- But since Oxalic Acid exists with 2 molecules of water, hence molecular weight of Oxalic acid $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)=126$
- Now, Equivalent weight = Molecular weight/Basicity
- Therefore, Equivalent Weight $=126 / 2=63$ (As 2 is the basicity)
- Basicity here means Oxalic Acid release $2 \mathrm{H}^{+}$ ions

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q:
Consider the following Statements about a solenoid :
1. The magnetic field strength in a solenoid depends upon the number of turns per unit length in the solenoid
2. The magnetic field strength in a solenoid depends upon the current flowing in the wire of the solenoid
3. The magnetic field strength in a solenoid depends upon the diameter of the solenoid
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is proportional to both the applied current and the number of turns per unit length. There is no dependence on the diameter of the solenoid, and the field strength doesn't depend on the position inside the solenoid, i.e., the field inside is constant.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of conducting tissue in plants ?
questions.solution: The pericycle is a cylinder of parenchyma or sclerenchyma cells. The pericycle is located between the endodermis and phloem in plant roots. The pericycle regulates the formation of lateral roots by rapidly dividing near the xylem elements of the root. Pericycle is not a component of conducting tissue in plants.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Light year is a unit of measurement of
options: amount of light received on earth in a year
questions.solution: A light-year is a unit of very large distance. It is the distance that light can travel in one year. Light moves at a velocity of about 300,000 kilometers $(\mathrm{km})$ each second. So in one year, it can travel about 10 trillion km.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following cell organelles does NOT possess its own genetic material encoding proteins ?
questions.solution: The ribosome is a complex made of protein and RNA and which adds up to numerous million Daltons in size and assumes an important part in the course of decoding the genetic message reserved in the genome into protein. In 1955, George E. Palade discovered ribosomes. Ribosomes can be found floating within the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following forces is non-central and non-conservative?
questions.solution: Non-conservative forces are dissipative forces such as friction or air resistance. These forces take energy away from the system as the system progresses, energy that you can't get back. These forces are path dependent; therefore it matters where the object starts and stops.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: On exposure to moist air, copper gains a green coat on its surface due to formation of which one of the following compounds ?
questions.solution:
Copper metal when exposed to air turns green in colour due to corrosion. When copper vessel is exposed to air in rainy season, the metal reacts with gases and moisture and atmospheric gases to form a mixture of copper carbonate and copper hydroxide. This gives a green colour to the surface of copper metal.
The reaction is as follows:
$2 \mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{OH})_2+\mathrm{CuCO}_3$

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following organisms represents the primary consumer category in an ecosystem?
questions.solution: Caterpillars are the larval stage of members of the order Lepidoptera. Caterpillars, is a organism represent the primary consumer category in an ecosystem. Most caterpillars have cylindrical bodies consisting of multiple segments, with three pairs of true legs on the thorax and several pairs of short, fleshy prolegs on the abdomen.

- Air is a mixture of primarily Nitrogen and Oxygen gas.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: Which one of the following will NOT produce carbon dioxide on reacting with an aqueous solution of hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
In the given options, marble, limestone, and baking soda are all either metal carbonates or bicarbonates. All these when react with a dilute acid then they produce carbon dioxide. Whereas lime which is calcium oxide when react with a dilute acid then they do not produce carbon dioxide.
For example, $\mathrm{CaO}+$ dil. $2 \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaCl}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
Thus, lime when reacts with an acid then it produces salt and water but it does not produce carbon dioxide.

questions.solution: Binder refers to substances that hold the particles of pigment together in paint.

questions.q: Basic scientific principle behind a nuclear reactor is
questions.solution: Nuclear reactors operate on the principle of nuclear fission, the process in which a heavy atomic nucleus splits into two smaller fragments. The nuclear fragments are in very excited states and emit neutrons, other subatomic particles, and photons.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: 'Black hole' is a
options: huge black star which has zero acceleration due to gravity on its surface
star which has moderate acceleration due to gravity on its surface
star which has collapsed into itself and has large acceleration due to gravity on its surface
star which has collapsed into itself and has zero acceleration due to gravity on its surface

questions.q: Two metallic wires $A$ and $B$ are made using copper. The radius of wire $A$ is $r$ while its length is $l$. The radius of wire $B$ is $2 r$, and its length is $2 l$ and the same dc voltage $V$ is applied across it causing power dissipation $P_1$. Which one of the following is the correct relationship between $P$ and $P_1$ ?
questions.solution:
Resis tance of wire $\mathrm{R}=\rho \frac{l}{\mathrm{~A}}=\rho \cdot \frac{l}{\pi \mathrm{r}^2}$
If $R_0$ is resistance of first wire, the resistance of second wire.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=\rho \cdot \frac{2 l}{\pi \cdot(2 \mathrm{r})^2}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \rho \frac{l}{\pi \mathrm{r}^2}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_0}{2} \\ & \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{R}_0} \text { and } \mathrm{P}_1=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{R}_{0 / 2}}=2 \mathrm{P}\end{aligned}$

options: These are dead tissues and form wood
They provide flexibility to plant due to their thickened walls
These are present in the bark of a tree only
Growth occurs in plants due to division of cells of these tissues
questions.solution: Meristematic tissues, or simply meristems, are tissues in which the cells remain forever young and divide actively throughout the life of the plant. Cells within the meristematic tissues are self-renewing, so that each time they divide, one cell remains identical to the parent while the other can specialize and become part of another plant structure. The meristematic tissue is therefore self-sustaining.

options: Thallophytes have well differentiated body design
Vascular system is not found among Bryophytes
questions.solution:
Mosses and liverworts are lumped together as bryophytes, plants lacking true vascular tissues, and sharing a number of other primitive traits. They also lack true stems, roots, or leaves, though they have cells that perform these general functions.
Bryophytes do not have a true vascular system and are unable to pull water and nutrients up from the ground at any significant distance. Lacking this specialised system distinguishes bryophytes from ferns and flowering plants. It is for this reason that they are considered to be rather primitive plants.

questions.solution:
kWh (kilowatt-hour) and Joules are two energy units. 1 watt is defined as 1 joule/second. So if you multiply a watt times seconds, you get Ws which is also a joule.
So 1 kW is 1000 W , and an hour is 60 seconds x 60 minutes.
So $1 \mathrm{kWh}=3600 \mathrm{kWs}=3,600,000 \mathrm{Ws}=3,600,000 \mathrm{~J}$

This virus causes bone marrow suppression leading to reduction in number of blood platelets. A typical person has a platelet count of between 150,000 and 250,000 per microlitre of blood. About 80 to 90 per cent of patients with dengue will have levels below 100,000 , while 10 to 20 per cent of patients will see critically low levels of 20,000 or less.

questions.q: Which one of the following elements corrodes rapidly?
questions.solution: Iron corrodes rapidly, because of its non-stable corrosion products on the surface. Rust occurs when metals containing iron react with the oxygen in the air or in water and form a compound called iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide). This compound contains water molecules, so we call it a hydrated compound. Both oxygen gas and water must be present for the iron to rust. Chemically and very simply speaking, iron atoms lose a few electrons to oxygen atoms. This process by which electrons are removed from atoms is called oxidation. When oxidation occurs, it produces a chemical reaction that creates iron(III) oxide-or rust.

options: total number of protons in an atom
total number of neutrons is an atom
total number of electrons in the outer most shell of an atom
questions.solution: Valency is the measure of the combining capacity of atoms or molecules. Therefore, it is the capacity of an atom of a single element to react and combine with particular numbers of atoms of another element. The electrons present in the outermost shell/orbit of an atom are called valence electrons. The valence electrons take part in any chemical reaction because the outermost orbit usually contains more energy than the electrons present in other orbits. The valency of an element depends upon the total number of electrons in the outer most shell of an atom.

Red blood cells (RBCs) have no nucleus, no mitochondria and no endoplasmic reticulum. Hemoglobin is the protein inside red blood cells. It carries oxygen. Red blood cells also remove carbon dioxide from human body. Foods rich in iron help you maintain healthy red blood cells. Vitamins are also needed to build healthy red blood cells.

questions.subject: General Ability
questions.q: In a solenoid, the current flowing through the wire is I and number of turns per unit length is $n$. This gives a magnetic field $B$ inside the solenoid. If number of turn per unit length is increased to 2 n , what will be the value of magnetic field in the solenoid?
questions.solution:
A long solenoid is the one which has a larger length in comparison to the radius. It consists of a long wire wound in the form of a helix where the neighboring turns are closely spaced. So each turn can be regarded as a circular loop. The net magnetic field is the vector sum of the fields due to all the turns. Enamelled wires are used for winding so that turns are insulated from each other.
The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is: $\mathrm{B}=\mu_0 \mathrm{nI}\ldots \ldots \ldots$. (1) where $\mathrm{n}=$ number of turns per unit length and $\mathrm{I}=$ current flowing through the solenoid. The magnetic field at a point on one end of the long solenoid is: $\mathrm{B}=\left(\mu_0 \mathrm{nI} / 2\right)$

questions.q: A body has a free fall from a height of 20 m . After falling through a distance of 5 m , the body would
options: lose one-fourth of its total energy

gain one-fourth of its potential energy
gain three-fourth of its total energy
questions.solution:
According to law of conservation of energy total energy remains conserved.
$\text { P.E. }=\mathrm{mgh}=20 \mathrm{mg}$
Loss in potential energy is observed, as
$\begin{aligned}
& (\text { P.E. })^1=\mathrm{mgh}=5 \mathrm{mg} \\
& (\text { P.E })^1 /(\text { P.E })=5 \mathrm{mg} / 20 \mathrm{mg}=1 / 4 \\
& (\text { P.E. })^1=1 / 4 \text { P.E }
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two bodies A and B are moving with equal velocities. The mass of $B$ is double that of $A$. In this context, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Momentum of B will be double that of A.
Momentum of A will be double that of B.
Momentum of B will be four times that of A.
Momenta of both A and B will be equal.
questions.solution:
As we know
Momentum $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{mv}$
Since, $V_A=V_B=V$, and $m_0=2 m_A$
for $A, \quad P_A=m_A v_A$
for B $\quad P_B=\left(2 m_A\right) v_A\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=2 \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}$

Mass is an invariant quantity. Acceleration due to gravity (g) decreases with altitude as one rises above the Earth's surface because greater altitude means greater distance from the Earth's centre.
Weight, $\mathrm{w}=$ mass $(\mathrm{m}) \times$ acc. due to gravity $(\mathrm{g})\mathrm{g}_{\text {height }}=\mathrm{g} /\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)^2$
Hence body weighs less on hill top than on earth's
surface.

questions.q: If radius of the earth were to shrink by $1 \%$, its mass remaining the same, g would decrease by nearly
questions.solution:
If the radius of the earth were to shrink by one percent, mass remaining the same, the value of $g$ will increase by $2 \%$.
$\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}^2}$
If mass remains constant, then $\mathrm{g} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{R}^2}\begin{aligned}
& \% ~\text { increase in } g=2(\% ~\text { decrease in } \mathrm{R}) \\
& =2 \times 1 \%=2 \%
\end{aligned}$
Therefore value of g will increase by $2 \%$.

the flask, and if enough is placed in the flask to cover
the bottom, it exhibits a strongly convex meniscus,
whereas the meniscus of water is concave. Mercury will
not wet the glass, unlike water and many other liquids,
and if the glass is tipped, it will 'roll' around inside.

questions.q:
The sun is observed to be reddish when it is near the horizon,
i.e., in the morning and the evening. This is because
options: red light is least scattered by atmosphere
red light is most scattered by atmosphere
it is the colour of the Sun in the morning and evening
questions.solution:
Tiny molecules in our atmosphere cause light to scatter. That's why our sky looks blue: it's because the atmosphere scatters the bluish component of white sunlight. And it's why the sun looks reddish when it's near the horizon. Sunlight encounters more air molecules when the sun is low in the sky than when the sun is overhead. Even more blue light is scattered away, leaving mostly the reddish scattering
$\propto \frac{1}{\lambda^4}$ component of white sunlight to travel the straighter path to your eyes. So the setting and rising sun looks red.

questions.q:
When you walk on a woolen carpet and bring your finger
near the metallic handle of a door an electric shock is
produced. This is because
options: charge is transferred from your body to the handle
a chemical reaction occurs when you touch the handle
the temperature of the human body is higher than that of the handle
the human body and the handle arrive at thermal equilibrium by the process
questions.solution:
All materials are made up of negatively- and positivelycharged particles. These usually exist in equal amounts, balancing each other out. But when two materials come into contact, one may 'steal' negatively-charged
electrons from the other. One material ends up with more negative charges than positive ones, meaning that it becomes negatively-charged overall, whilst the other becomes positively-charged. If the charges cannot move away as they are produced, they accumulate in the material as static charge, or electricity. Once you have built up a big enough static charge, an electric shock is almost inevitable. The moment you touch a conducting material such as metal, the excess electrons jump between your hand and the conductor, giving you a shock.

questions.solution:
In isothermal process
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta \mathrm{T}=0 \\
& \therefore \quad P V=\text { Constant } \\
& \mathrm{P} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~V}}
\end{aligned}$
From $\quad \mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1=\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2$
here $\quad \mathrm{P}_2=\left(1+\frac{10}{100}\right) \mathrm{P}_1=1.1 \mathrm{P}_1\therefore$ Change in volume
$\frac{V_1-V_2}{V_1}=\frac{1}{11}$
Percentage decrease $=9.09 \%$.
